says: For every y in [0,1]^146 whose mass m(y) = Σ_i w_i y_i lies in [2/5, 9/20], L_θ(y) ≥ 50963377393403307885655938/185520059131196374275938963885, where L_θ is the minorant of CERT-FORMAT.md built from the model of φ* on this grid and the certificate's θ (θ_t attached to the t-th cut pair in lexicographic order).

data.reading: every rational is the JSON string "p/q" or "p", read as the exact rational it denotes; a pair (i, j) is ordered (a in I_i, b in I_j); the forms are a multiset (Σ μ_f f does not depend on their order), each (kind, idx, μ) kept as written — yy [i, j] and yy [j, i] are two entries.

thetaPairs.what: the ordered cut pair each θ_t is attached to: 0 < A_in < w_i w_j (CERT-FORMAT.md), A_in computed exactly

proof.what: the certificate's reason, checked by each kernel's checker; not part of what is claimed

lean.bound: HOLE: no Lean statement of the bound exists (no soundness theorem for checkWith); PLAN.md §5

outside: the model constants: a_i, b_i (bathtub), the signs s_i of φ*, the areas A_in — HOL4 takes them as data (export.js from the JavaScript verifier's gridData), Lean's checker computes them from φ*'s twelve blocks; compared here as data, never part of the claim
the witness: HOL4 D, T, d, Lw; Lean slabWitness (geo, heights, summaries, matrix, scales, factor, margins) — untrusted hints; a wrong one can only make a checker refuse
the analysis: E(σ) ≥ L(y) (centring, bathtub, discretisation), the cover of [0, 1/2], E(σ) = E(1 − σ), PRS Lemma 1 — in neither kernel
the meaning of Lean's `check slabCert = true`: no Lean theorem says acceptance implies the bound
